name: IN-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Messmer running with a large fundraising edge
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~3%
No public polling of the race
model.rationale: Messmer holds a heavily Republican seat, out-raised Allen roughly four-to-one, and markets give Democrats only about a 3% chance; nothing in the evidence suggests moving off the fundamentals-based Safe R call.
model.watch: A major late Democratic outside-spending surge or an unexpected scandal involving Messmer could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Indiana's 8th District is a solidly Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about 18 points toward the GOP. First-term incumbent Mark Messmer is running for reelection after clearing his primary, and he holds a substantial financial advantage, having raised over $1.1 million and keeping more than $700,000 on hand. Democratic challenger Mary Allen has raised under $300,000, leaving her with limited resources for a district that favors Republicans strongly.

No public general-election polling is available, and no expert raters have flagged the race as competitive. Prediction markets give Democrats only about a 3% chance of winning. With the incumbent, the district lean, and the money gap all pointing the same direction, the race is rated Safe Republican, with modest uncertainty given the absence of polling.
